title: India’s foreign-investment census shows why inward and outward positions converged
summary: India’s inward direct investment was 4.2 times its outward investment at end-March 2026, down from 5.5 times a year earlier in rupee terms. The Reserve Bank’s November 6 census explains why that comparison cannot be read as a verdict on investors withdrawing money. Each number is an outstanding position. Exchange-rate movements and changes in the value of equity can change the ratio without a cross-border transaction. Identifying the source of the convergence requires looking separately at the entities, instruments and valuation bases behind each side.

The census covers Indian companies, limited liability partnerships, alternative investment funds and partnerships reporting direct investment in either direction. Of 43,123 reporting entities, 34,845 reported inward investment only, 6,955 outward only and 1,323 both. A total of 36,127 had also reported in the preceding census. The difference in coverage limits year-over-year comparisons. New reporters can change a total while contributing little information about the behaviour of continuing firms. The RBI describes the 2025–26 results as provisional.

A count of firms, the nominal value of their issued equity and the current value of investors’ stakes give different pictures. About 97% of reporting entities were unlisted. They accounted for the larger part of inward direct-investment equity at face value, and non-financial companies accounted for more than 90% on that basis. At market value, however, listed and unlisted companies each represented close to half of inward equity. A small group of listed businesses can consequently represent a large portion of the foreign equity claim. Comparing capital recorded at face value in one group with market values in the other would misstate the concentration.

Debt was more concentrated outside public equity markets. Unlisted entities accounted for 96.6% of inward direct-investment debt. That measure refers to a direct-investment relationship. Table 4 separately identifies liabilities to unrelated non-residents, including loans, deposits, trade credit and other payables. Those liabilities rose 11.9% in rupees. Corresponding assets with unrelated non-residents rose 16.1%. These aggregate rates reveal neither the currencies and maturities of individual obligations nor whether the borrowers facing repayment are the same firms holding assets abroad.

The United States represented 16.5% of outstanding inward direct investment, followed by Mauritius at 14.5%, Singapore at 13.7% and the United Kingdom at 10.8%. Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and the United States together accounted for more than half of outward investment. Manufacturing accounted for 50.1% of the market value of inward direct-investment equity and services for 45%. The sector shares describe equity while the country shares concern direct investment more broadly. Their reported geographic distribution also need not trace a chain of intermediaries to the final owner.

The census thus identifies which claims could be sensitive to equity pricing, debt service or currency changes. To infer a change in demand for Indian assets, an analyst would need to reconcile opening and closing positions with actual transactions on a comparable reporting perimeter. The RBI explicitly distinguishes balance-of-payments flows from the changes in stocks shown here.

questions.question: How much of the lower inward-to-outward ratio reflects transactions?
questions.detail: Reconcile opening and closing positions separately in rupees and dollars. Start with the entities reporting in both censuses and add new respondents separately. Compare the unexplained change with equity prices and exchange rates before interpreting the result as a shift in foreign demand.

questions.question: Where would foreign-currency refinancing pressure first become visible?
questions.detail: Separate direct-investment borrowing from unrelated loans and trade credit. For unlisted borrowers, identify the obligation’s currency, maturity, related-party funding arrangements and revenue denomination. The unlisted debt share locates an exposure but says little about the timing of cash needs.

questions.question: Would outward investments make funding stress easier for inward borrowers to absorb?
questions.detail: Begin with the 1,323 reporting entities with both kinds of investment. Match liquidity, currency and the ability to transfer funds between affiliates. A foreign asset held by an unrelated firm can offer almost no protection to a domestic borrower facing a payment.

questions.question: Does the apparent concentration survive a consistent valuation basis?
questions.detail: Calculate comparable manufacturing and services shares from continuing firms. Test changes in source and destination countries against changes in corporate control and funding. The reported immediate counterparty can change without an equivalent change in who ultimately bears the risk.

limitation: The figures are provisional. Changes in positions include valuation and exchange-rate effects, and the census does not provide an ultimate-ownership or transaction bridge.
